takeover_reason: The single-entity CPU detector reported a high-grade deviation with sufficient confidence and the abnormal CPU level persisted across consecutive observations, so the anomaly was accepted for autonomous investigation.

agent_events.reason: A high-grade single-entity CPU anomaly exceeded the triage criteria and persisted across consecutive observations.
agent_events.outcome: Incident opened and initial infrastructure validation assigned to the System Engineer.

agent_events.reason: The Technical Lead requires host and container evidence before involving application specialists.
agent_events.outcome: CPU approximately 392%; memory stable; processing-service container running.

agent_events.action: Check host pressure and container health
agent_events.reason: The incident must be separated from host-wide resource exhaustion or a container runtime failure.
agent_events.outcome: No host-wide memory or disk pressure; CPU saturation is concentrated on processing-service.

agent_events.action: Inspect application logs and service health
agent_events.reason: Infrastructure evidence confirms the anomaly but does not explain whether the application is failing or simply processing excessive workload.
agent_events.outcome: No critical exceptions or crash loops; requests continue to complete successfully.

agent_events.reason: Application logs are healthy while CPU remains saturated, so abnormal incoming traffic must be tested as a competing hypothesis.
agent_events.outcome: Network Engineer consultation requested for request-rate and connection evidence.

agent_events.action: Correlate inbound traffic with CPU saturation
agent_events.reason: The Application Engineer needs to determine whether a traffic surge explains the workload increase.
agent_events.outcome: Inbound request volume increased sharply in the same window as processing-service CPU saturation.

agent_events.reason: A traffic increase must be distinguished from a connectivity problem that could produce retries or abnormal request amplification.
agent_events.outcome: No abnormal connection failures detected; evidence supports a workload surge rather than a network fault.

agent_events.reason: The application and network evidence point to workload saturation; the team needs to verify whether this behaviour is consistent with the processing-service design.
agent_events.outcome: Service documentation confirms CPU-bound processing under high request volume and recommends workload normalization before restart.

agent_events.reason: System, network and software evidence now converge and are sufficient to produce an evidence-backed diagnosis.
agent_events.outcome: Workload-induced CPU saturation diagnosed with confidence 0.88.

agent_events.action: Critically review diagnosis and hand incident to operator
agent_events.reason: The Technical Lead must verify that the specialist findings are consistent before presenting remediation guidance to the operator.
agent_events.outcome: Diagnosis accepted. Reduce abnormal workload, verify CPU recovery, and restart only if saturation persists. Incident moved to OPERATOR_ACTION_REQUIRED.

timeline.action: Confirm whether the OpenSearch anomaly reflects real runtime CPU saturation.
timeline.observation: processing-service CPU is approximately 392%; memory usage is stable and the container remains running.
timeline.decision_rationale: The anomaly is confirmed at runtime and is concentrated on processing-service.

timeline.action: Inspect recent application logs for exceptions, crash loops or repeated failures.
timeline.observation: No critical application error is present. Processing requests continue successfully while CPU remains saturated.
timeline.decision_rationale: The absence of application errors lowers the likelihood of an exception-driven failure.

timeline.action: Correlate inbound request behaviour with the CPU anomaly.
timeline.observation: Inbound workload increased sharply during the same time window in which CPU rose from baseline to sustained saturation.
timeline.decision_rationale: The traffic increase supports a workload hypothesis and no network path failure is observed.

timeline.action: Retrieve processing-service documentation and expected CPU behaviour.
timeline.observation: The service documentation describes CPU-bound processing under high request volume and recommends workload normalization before restart.
timeline.decision_rationale: The observed runtime behaviour is consistent with the documented implementation.

timeline.action: Validate the cross-specialist evidence before operator handoff.
timeline.observation: System, application, network and software findings are mutually consistent.
timeline.decision_rationale: Evidence is sufficient to accept workload-induced CPU saturation as the most probable cause.
timeline.outcome: Incident transferred to the operator with remediation guidance.

diagnosis.summary: The processing-service is CPU-saturated because of an abnormal increase in processing workload rather than an application crash, host resource failure or network connectivity fault.
evidence: System Engineer confirmed runtime CPU near 392% while memory and host pressure remained normal.
Application Engineer found no critical exceptions or crash-loop evidence.
Network Engineer confirmed a sharp inbound request increase without connection failures.
Software Developer verified that CPU-bound behaviour under high workload matches the documented processing-service design.
Technical Lead found no contradiction across the specialist reports.

alternatives.name: Host resource exhaustion
alternatives.reason: Memory, disk and host-wide resource pressure remained normal.

alternatives.name: Application exception loop
alternatives.reason: No repeated errors or crash-loop messages were present in recent application logs.

alternatives.name: Network connectivity failure
alternatives.reason: Request volume increased but no abnormal connection failure was observed.

remediation.summary: Reduce the abnormal input workload first, verify CPU recovery, and restart processing-service only if saturation persists after workload normalization.

steps.title: Confirm the active CPU saturation
steps.description: From the Windows host, capture the current container resource snapshot before changing the workload.

steps.title: Inspect and reduce the abnormal workload
steps.description: Check the traffic-generator scenario and stop or return it to the normal profile if the increase is not expected.

steps.title: Observe recovery before restarting
steps.description: Wait for the processing queue to drain and confirm that CPU returns close to its learned baseline.

steps.title: Restart only if saturation persists
steps.description: If CPU remains abnormally high after workload normalization, restart processing-service and continue monitoring for recurrence.

verification: processing-service CPU returns close to the normal learned range
request processing remains successful after workload normalization
no new high-grade CPU anomaly is generated by the single-entity detector
application logs remain free of new critical errors
risks: Stopping the traffic generator changes the workload and should be done only when the current traffic increase is not intentional.
Restarting processing-service can interrupt in-flight processing and should remain a secondary action after workload reduction.
